subject: Latency SLO addendum request - Helixa production bursts
messages:
From: Sasha Li <sasha.li@helixa.com>

Cc: Tom Greene <t.greene@helixa.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency commitments + daytime marketing bursts (Helixa)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We're close to sign-off but need to resolve one SLO item before procurement can finalize: daytime marketing pushes create predictable bursts in our traffic (30-45 min windows) that skew p95 measurements. Our legal/procurement team is asking whether Redwood can either:

- Provide a limited daytime carveout for scheduled marketing pushes, or
- Accept a relaxed p95 target during known burst windows and keep stricter p95 for steady-state traffic.

For context I've attached a short packet with our typical push windows and a 7-day sample of request traces (traffic_samples.csv). Our current ask (from procurement): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 600ms, measured on a rolling 60-minute window, but with an explicit allowance for up to 6 hours/month of scheduled burst carveouts.

Can Redwood propose a contractual addendum that covers either of the above? If useful, Tom and I can carve out 30 minutes for a call tomorrow to walk through the traces.

Attachments: helixa_slo_request.pdf; traffic_samples.csv

Thanks,
Sasha Li
Head of Platform Operations, Helixa
Sasha.Li@helixa.com
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency commitments + daytime marketing bursts (Helixa)

Hi Sasha — thanks for the packet, got it. Short answer: yes, we can work with you on a limited, documented carveout approach, but we need to be explicit about scope and observability to avoid open-ended exceptions.

Two quick items from our side:
1) Measurement model: we typically run p50 on a rolling 5-minute aggregation and p95 on a rolling 60-minute aggregation for hosted API commitments. We can propose an alternative that preserves steady-state p95 while allowing for documented, scheduled carveouts.
2) Carveout governance: we propose a schedule-driven carveout (Helixa provides a schedule + 72h notice) limited to X hours per month and capped per event so it can't be used as a general waiver.

If that sounds reasonable I'll loop in Product (Lauren) and our Pricing lead (Ben) and draft an initial addendum for your review. Would 10am PST Monday (Apr 19) work for a 30-minute screen share to walk the traces? Calendar invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=helixa-meeting-20270419

Best,

Would Redwood consider a hard cap (e.g., 8 hours/month) combined with a reduced p95 target during those events?

I've attached the tentative push calendar (push_schedule.xlsx). If Redwood prefers a single approach, we can accept a higher p95 during pushes if it helps close the deal faster.

[push_schedule.xlsx attached]

Lauren / Ben — proposed internal terms:
- Baseline commitments (steady-state): p50 <= 150ms (rolling 5m), p95 <= 650ms (rolling 60m).
- Scheduled-burst carveout: up to 8 hours/month total, events must be declared with 72h notice, each event capped at 2 hours. During carveouts p95 target relaxes to <= 900ms.
- Credit/backstop: if steady-state p95 exceeds 650ms outside declared carveouts for more than 3 consecutive measurement windows, Redwood to provide service credits (TBD %) or mitigation plan.

Recommendation from Product: accept baseline commitments above, offer carveout at 6 hours/month with event cap 90 minutes, and require explicit per-event notice + post-event traffic logs for audit. Draft addendum attached: proposed_addendum_redwood.pdf

Thoughts? I'm comfortable moving this to a short addendum that both parties sign.

Lauren Bishop
VP Product — Redwood Inference

Hi Sasha / Tom — thanks for the meeting and for the schedule. Attached is our counterproposal (redwood_slo_addendum.docx) that balances predictability for Helixa with guardrails for the hosted fleet. Key points below so they're easy to scan: 

- Baseline (steady-state) commitments: p50 <= 150ms (rolling 5-minute aggregation); p95 <= 700ms (rolling 60-minute aggregation).
- Scheduled-burst carveout: up to 6 hours/month total; individual events capped at 90 minutes; Helixa to provide 72 hours notice with event window and expected peak QPS. During carveout windows the contractual p95 commitment relaxes to <= 900ms.
- Observability & audit: Helixa will provide traffic logs for each declared event within 24 hours post-event. Redwood will publish per-event measurements and a scoped audit report on request.
- Mitigation & credits: Any steady-state p95 breach outside declared carveouts that persists across 3 consecutive 60-minute windows triggers a remediation runbook plus a service credit equal to 10% of monthly hosted inference spend for the impacted tenant for that billing month (subject to the addendum's definitions).
- Term & termination: Addendum is a 12-month rider to the standard TOS with mutual 30-day termination.

Next steps: If that looks good, I'll open a DocuSign (link below) for an initial 12-month rider. If you need an alternate numeric for the credit %, flag it now and we can iterate. DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/HLX-089

Thanks again — we'll stand by for final confirmation.

Best,
Priyom Das
